Recipe 01 · Breakfast

Sausage, Egg & Cheese Pancake Bake

Savory sausage, fluffy eggs and melted cheddar baked with pieces of pancake. Serve it with maple syrup, hot sauce or salsa.

Prep15 minutes
Bake30–35 minutes
Serves6–8 people

The finished bake should be golden on top and firm in the center.

What you need

  • 1 pound ground breakfast sausage (one standard package)
  • 6 large eggs
  • 1 cup milk (whole or 2%)
  • 6–8 pancakes, about 6 inches wide
  • 2 tablespoons butter, melted, plus more for the dish
  • 2 cups shredded cheddar cheese (one 8-ounce bag)
  • 1 teaspoon salt
  • ½ teaspoon black pepper
  • ½ teaspoon garlic powder
  • ¼ teaspoon paprika
  • ¼ teaspoon onion powder (optional)

Also grab: a 9 × 13-inch baking dish, a skillet, a mixing bowl, a whisk and a spatula.

How to make it

  1. Heat the oven to 375°F. Rub a little butter all over the inside of a 9 × 13-inch baking dish.
  2. Cook the sausage. Put it in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook for 8–10 minutes, breaking it into small crumbles with a spatula. When there is no pink left, carefully drain off the grease.
  3. Build the first layer. Tear the pancakes into bite-size pieces and spread them evenly across the bottom of the baking dish.
  4. Mix the eggs. Whisk the eggs, milk, salt, pepper, garlic powder, paprika and onion powder together in a large bowl. Pour the mixture evenly over the pancakes.
  5. Add the toppings. Scatter the cooked sausage over the dish. Cover it with the shredded cheese, then drizzle the melted butter over the top.
  6. Bake for 30–35 minutes. It is done when the center does not jiggle and the top is golden. If you use a food thermometer, the center should reach 160°F.
  7. Let it rest for 5 minutes. Cut it into squares and serve while it is warm.

How to serve it

Maple syrup gives it a sweet-and-savory taste. Hot sauce or salsa works when you want more bite.

Save the leftovers

Cover and refrigerate for up to 3–4 days. Reheat one serving at a time until it is hot all the way through.

Recipe 02 · Breakfast

Thomas's Loaded Breakfast Burritos

Crispy potatoes, savory sausage, soft scrambled eggs and melty cheddar rolled up in a warm tortilla. Makes eight big burritos that reheat perfectly.

Prep15 minutes
Cook25 minutes
TotalAbout 40 minutes
Makes8 burritos

Roll them tight, then toast the seam so every burrito stays together.

What you need

  • 8 large flour tortillas (10-inch)
  • 8 large eggs
  • ½ pound ground breakfast sausage (or 6 strips of bacon)
  • 2 cups frozen hash browns (or 2 medium potatoes, diced small)
  • 1½ cups shredded cheddar cheese
  • 2 tablespoons butter
  • 1 teaspoon salt
  • ½ teaspoon black pepper
  • ½ teaspoon garlic powder
  • ¼ teaspoon paprika
  • Salsa for serving (optional)

Also grab: a large skillet, a mixing bowl, a whisk and a spatula.

How to make them

  1. Crisp the potatoes. Melt 1 tablespoon of butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the hash browns for 8–10 minutes, stirring now and then, until crispy and golden. Season with half of the salt, pepper, garlic powder and paprika. Scoop them out and set aside.
  2. Cook the sausage. In the same skillet, brown the sausage over medium heat for 8–10 minutes, breaking it into crumbles. Drain the grease, then set the sausage aside with the potatoes.
  3. Scramble the eggs. Melt the other tablespoon of butter over medium-low heat. Whisk the eggs with the rest of the seasonings. Scramble gently until the eggs are just set and still soft.
  4. Warm the tortillas. Heat them in a dry skillet or the microwave just until soft. This keeps them from cracking when you roll them.
  5. Build each burrito. Put a scoop of potatoes, sausage and eggs down the center, then add a handful of cheese. Fold in the two sides and roll it up tight.
  6. Toast them if you like. Put each burrito seam-side down in a dry hot skillet for 1–2 minutes per side. This seals the burrito and gives it a crisp finish.

Keep them for later

Wrap each burrito in foil. Keep them in the fridge for 3–4 days or in the freezer for up to one month.

Reheat them

Use the microwave or oven until hot all the way through. Take the foil off before putting a burrito in the microwave.

Recipe 03 · Lunch

Thomas's Crispy Chicken Bacon Ranch Wraps

Crunchy breaded chicken, crispy bacon, melty cheese, fresh lettuce and tomato, and cool ranch wrapped up in a toasted tortilla. Makes four big wraps.

Prep20 minutes
Cook15 minutes
TotalAbout 35 minutes
Makes4 wraps

Toast the seam first so the wraps stay closed and get crisp on the outside.

What you need

  • 4 large flour tortillas (10-inch)
  • 1 pound chicken tenders (or 2 chicken breasts cut into strips)
  • 1 cup flour
  • 2 eggs, beaten
  • 1½ cups breadcrumbs (or crushed cornflakes for extra crunch)
  • 1 teaspoon salt
  • ½ teaspoon black pepper
  • ½ teaspoon garlic powder
  • ½ teaspoon paprika
  • Vegetable oil for frying (about 1 cup)
  • 8 strips bacon, cooked crispy
  • 1 cup shredded cheddar or Monterey Jack cheese
  • 2 cups shredded lettuce
  • 1 large tomato, diced
  • ½ cup ranch dressing, plus more for dipping

Also grab: three shallow bowls, a large skillet, tongs and paper towels.

How to make them

  1. Set up the breading station. Put the flour, salt, pepper, garlic powder and paprika in the first bowl. Put the beaten eggs in the second and the breadcrumbs in the third.
  2. Bread the chicken. Dip each tender in the flour, then the egg, then the breadcrumbs. Press the crumbs onto the chicken so they stick.
  3. Fry until crisp. Heat about ½ inch of oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Fry the chicken for 3–4 minutes per side, until golden and cooked through. Move it to paper towels to drain.
  4. Warm the tortillas. Heat them in a dry skillet or the microwave just until soft so they roll without cracking.
  5. Build each wrap. Spread ranch down the center, then add lettuce, tomato, 2 chicken tenders, 2 bacon strips and a handful of cheese. Fold in the sides and roll it up tight.
  6. Toast the wraps. Put each one seam-side down in a dry skillet for 1–2 minutes per side, until golden and the cheese melts.

Best served fresh

These wraps are at their crispiest right out of the skillet. Serve with extra ranch for dipping.

Keep the chicken

Refrigerate cooked chicken for up to 3 days and build the wraps when you're ready. Don't store them assembled with lettuce or they will get soggy.

Recipe 04 · Lunch

Thomas's All-American Burger Basket

A diner-style spread with juicy cheeseburgers, crispy seasoned fries and a thick vanilla shake. Makes four servings.

Prep20 minutes
Cook30 minutes
TotalAbout 50 minutes
Serves4 people

Make the shake last so it stays cold and thick when the burgers and fries are ready.

What you need

  • For the burgers
  • 1 pound ground beef (one standard package)
  • 1 teaspoon salt
  • ½ teaspoon black pepper
  • ½ teaspoon garlic powder
  • ½ teaspoon onion powder
  • 4 slices cheddar cheese
  • 4 burger buns
  • Lettuce, tomato, onion, pickles, ketchup, mustard and mayo
  • For the fries
  • 3 large russet potatoes (or one bag of frozen fries)
  • 2 tablespoons vegetable oil
  • 1 teaspoon salt
  • ½ teaspoon paprika
  • ¼ teaspoon garlic powder
  • For the shake
  • 3 cups vanilla ice cream
  • 1 cup milk
  • 2 tablespoons chocolate syrup (optional)
  • Whipped cream (optional)

Also grab: a baking sheet, a large skillet or grill, a spatula and a blender.

How to make it

  1. Start with the fries—they take the longest. Heat the oven to 425°F. Cut the potatoes into thin strips, then toss them with the oil, salt, paprika and garlic powder. Spread them in one layer on a baking sheet. Bake for 25–30 minutes, flipping once halfway through, until golden and crispy.
  2. Make the patties. Gently mix the salt, pepper, garlic powder and onion powder into the ground beef. Don't overwork it. Form four patties, then press your thumb into the center of each one so they don't puff up.
  3. Cook the burgers. Put the patties in a hot skillet or on the grill for 3–4 minutes per side. Add a slice of cheese during the last minute so it melts. Toast the buns cut-side down in the skillet.
  4. Build the burgers. Add your favorite toppings and sauces to each one.
  5. Make the shake last so it stays thick. Blend the ice cream, milk and chocolate syrup, if you're using it, for about 30 seconds. Pour into tall glasses and add whipped cream if you like.

Best served fresh

Bring the burgers, hot fries and cold shakes to the table as soon as everything is ready.

Save the leftovers

Cooked patties keep in the fridge for 3 days. Reheat fries in the oven or air fryer to crisp them back up—the microwave makes them soggy.
